cases.title: Scenario 1: Batasan Hills outage, cause and restoration time

grade.notes: Replies were short, spoken-friendly, and followed the style: sentence-first answers, tool lead-in lines, a proper goodbye, and no banned words. English-led Taglish with po, "Sandali lang po", and "Verified na po kayo" suited a Tagalog-mixed caller, and she gave the cause and restoration time without extra detail. She was courteous throughout, with "Sorry to hear that po" and "You're welcome po".

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hello po. Wala pong internet ang bahay namin since kaninang umaga. Gusto ko lang pong malaman kung bakit at kailan babalik.

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: Sorry to hear that po. May I have your Kidlat Fiber account number and the last four digits of your registered mobile number so I can verify your account?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Opo, ang account number ko po ay ******5601. Tapos yung last four digits ng mobile number ay 0101.

transcript.speaker: tala

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: Verified na po kayo, Maria. Let me check your area for outages now.

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: There's an outage in your area po, caused by a fiber cable cut along Batasan Road during road works. Service is expected back by around 2:23 AM tomorrow, Saturday. Would you like the outage reference number po?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Ah, ganun po ba, na-cut po pala yung fiber cable dahil sa road works. Sige po, naiintindihan ko na, hihintayin ko na lang hanggang 2:23 AM bukas. Salamat po sa tulong, Tala. Paalam po!

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: You're welcome po, Maria. Thank you for calling Kidlat Fiber.

cases.title: Scenario 3: slow internet, a reboot that does not fix it, a technician visit

input.notes: Customer reports slow internet for two days with video calls freezing. Diagnostics found high signal loss on the fiber line, modem degraded. Remote restart was tried and the fault remained.

grade.notes: Replies are mostly short, spoken-friendly, and English-led with natural 'po' and 'Sandali lang po', and she avoids 'Naku' and 'Walang anuman'. A few turns run long (the technician windows turn and the reference-number turn) and the 'Sunday' option reads a bit list-like, and she only confirms the last four digits correctly. Overall she is courteous and keeps the call moving.
